subject: math.FA
name: Invariant subspace problem on Hilbert space
statement: Does every bounded linear operator on a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space have a closed invariant subspace other than {0} and the whole space?
importance: It is a foundational question about the internal structure of bounded operators.
status_note: Counterexamples on general Banach spaces do not answer the Hilbert-space problem; many special operator classes are known to have invariant subspaces.

subject: math.FA
name: Separable quotient problem
statement: Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space have an infinite-dimensional separable Banach quotient by a closed linear subspace?
importance: It asks whether every Banach space has a manageable infinite-dimensional linear image.
status_note: The assertion is known for large classes, including dual and reflexive spaces, but not for all Banach spaces.

references.title: On the separable quotient problem for Banach spaces
The Separable Quotient Problem and the Lotz Property in Banach Spaces

subject: math.FA
name: Mazur’s rotations problem
statement: Must a separable real Banach space whose surjective linear isometries act transitively on its unit sphere be linearly isometric to a Hilbert space?
importance: It asks whether maximal norm symmetry forces the geometry of an inner product.
status_note: Separability and exact transitivity are essential; almost transitivity has non-Hilbert examples.

references.title: On Mazur rotations problem and its multidimensional versions

subject: math.FA
name: Exact real Grothendieck constant
statement: Determine the least K such that, for every real matrix (aᵢⱼ) and real Hilbert-space unit vectors uᵢ,vⱼ, |Σaᵢⱼ⟨uᵢ,vⱼ⟩| ≤ K max_{εᵢ,ηⱼ∈{−1,1}} |Σaᵢⱼεᵢηⱼ|.
importance: The constant is central to tensor norms, operator theory, and semidefinite approximation algorithms.
status_note: Grothendieck’s inequality gives a finite constant; known upper and lower bounds do not determine the exact real value.

references.title: Braverman et al., The Grothendieck constant is strictly smaller than Krivine’s bound

subject: math.FA
name: Exact complex Grothendieck constant
statement: Determine the least K for the complex Grothendieck inequality: for every complex matrix (aᵢⱼ) and complex Hilbert-space unit vectors uᵢ,vⱼ, |Σaᵢⱼ⟨uᵢ,vⱼ⟩| ≤ K max_{|sᵢ|=|tⱼ|=1} |Σaᵢⱼsᵢtⱼ|.
importance: This distinct complex constant governs complex tensor norms and sharp operator inequalities.
status_note: Its exact value is unknown; current upper and lower bounds, including recent improvements, remain distinct.

references.title: Sharper Bounds for the Complex Grothendieck Constant

subject: math.FA
name: Symmetric Mahler conjecture
statement: For every origin-symmetric convex body K⊂ℝⁿ with n≥4, is vol(K) vol(K°) ≥ 4ⁿ/n!, where K°={y:⟨x,y⟩≤1 for all x∈K}?
importance: It predicts the sharp uncertainty between the size of a norm’s unit ball and that of its dual norm.
status_note: The low-dimensional cases and several special classes are proved; the general dimension-four-and-higher assertion remains open.

subject: math.FA
name: Four-dimensional Fourier restriction conjecture
statement: For every q>8/3, is there C_q such that ‖∫_{S³} e^{ix·ω} g(ω)dσ(ω)‖_{L^q(ℝ⁴)} ≤ C_q ‖g‖_{L∞(S³)} for every bounded measurable g?
importance: It predicts the sharp integrability gain created by Fourier extension from a curved hypersurface.
status_note: The exponent 8/3 is dictated by necessary examples. Existing restriction estimates do not cover the full proposed range.

references.title: Tao, Recent progress on the restriction conjecture

subject: math.FA
name: Three-dimensional Bochner–Riesz conjecture
statement: For every 1<p<∞ and δ>max{3|1/p−1/2|−1/2,0}, is the Fourier multiplier (1−|ξ|²)_+^δ bounded on Lᵖ(ℝ³)?
importance: It asks for the sharp convergence theory of multidimensional Fourier summation.
status_note: The proposed range is suggested by necessary conditions. Some exponent ranges are established, but the full three-dimensional assertion remains open.

subject: math.FA
name: Sharp Beurling–Ahlfors operator norm
statement: For 1<p<∞, is the norm of the Beurling–Ahlfors transform on Lᵖ(ℂ) exactly max{p,p/(p−1)}−1?
importance: It is a leading sharp-norm problem for singular integral operators with consequences for quasiconformal analysis.
status_note: The conjectured lower bound and the Hilbert-space case are known; the matching upper bound outside p=2 is open.

references.title: Bañuelos and Janakiraman, Lp-bounds for the Beurling–Ahlfors transform

subject: math.FA
name: Existence of boundedly distortable Banach spaces
statement: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional Banach space X that is λ₀-distortable for some λ₀>1 but fails to be λ-distortable for at least one λ>λ₀? Here λ-distortable means an equivalent norm forces, in every infinite-dimensional subspace, a ratio greater than λ between the new norms of two original-norm unit vectors.
importance: It asks whether distortion of infinite-dimensional Banach geometry can be nontrivial yet uniformly limited.
status_note: Nondistortable and arbitrarily distortable spaces are known; the intermediate bounded-distortion phenomenon is unresolved.

references.title: Asymptotic ℓp spaces and bounded distortions
